sentences.text: Software changes are managed through a controlled lifecycle that protects the integrity and availability of operational systems.
Each operational software component has an identified owner, approved version, and documented configuration baseline.
The baseline records software versions, configuration parameters, dependencies, and applicable hardware revisions.
Source code and configuration files are held in access-controlled repositories with revision history enabled.
Changes are developed and reviewed outside the live operational environment.
Release packages are built from approved source and checked for completeness, integrity, and compatibility.
The SCADA Engineer uses the Firmware Hash Attestation to verify the approved image before loading a release.
The Control Engineer confirms that proposed changes have a clear operational purpose and defined scope.
Technical approval is recorded before a change is scheduled for deployment to an operational system.
Reviewers assess safety effects, cybersecurity risks, interfaces, and the impact on ongoing maintenance activities.
Changes affecting protection functions or control behavior receive additional engineering scrutiny.
Testing is performed in a representative test environment before operational acceptance is considered.
The SCADA Gateway is checked for compatibility with the approved software and configuration baseline.
The Turbine Controller is tested against defined operating limits and expected fault responses.
The Pitch System is verified to retain its approved control behavior after an applicable software change.
The Converter Cabinet is checked for expected communication and protection behavior during regression testing.
Changes affecting the Offshore Substation are reviewed for consequences to the safe operation of connected equipment.
The Main Transformer protection settings remain subject to their separate engineering approval process.
The Cybersecurity Gateway is assessed for continued compliance with access controls and security requirements.
The Shore Control Room confirms that monitoring and operator procedures remain suitable for the revised configuration.
Deployment is scheduled for an approved maintenance window with qualified personnel available to supervise the work.
A rollback method is documented and checked before deployment begins.
If verification fails, the change is stopped and the affected system is returned to its last approved baseline where practicable.
Configuration records are updated after successful deployment, including the approval evidence, test results, and installed version.
Operational handover records identify the deployed change, any outstanding limitations, and the responsible technical contact.
